Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that there are two main questions related to the effects of intracerebroventricular injections of metformin and AICAR on melatonin secretion in ewes. To address these questions, we can synthesize a clear and concise answer as follows:

The injection of metformin or AICAR into the cerebral ventricles has been shown to affect melatonin levels in ewes. These substances are known to activate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), which plays a role in regulating metabolic processes.

It is likely that AMPK activation leads to an increase in plasma melatonin concentrations, as AMPK is involved in the regulation of the paraventricular nucleus and/or the pineal gland. This suggests that metformin or AICAR may act as a "metabolic cue" to modulate melatonin secretion.

In other words, the injection of these substances into the brain may influence the timing and amplitude of melatonin release, which could have implications for our understanding of the regulation of sleep-wake cycles in mammals.
